name: Cursor
$comment: osTested is deliberately empty. Cursor 3.18.25 is installed on the machine this was written on and its shipped bundle was read directly, which is why the grades below are `source` rather than `docs` — but nobody has yet driven LeastGrant inside a running Cursor session. Reading the binary is strong evidence about the contract and no evidence at all about the integration. That distinction is the whole reason this file separates `source` from `probe`.

allow.note: Observed on beforeReadFile: an ordinary project file returned allow and the read completed.

deny.note: Honoured on every surface, and stronger than the host’s own flow: a deny on a command Cursor would otherwise auto-run without prompting was blocked outright, with LeastGrant’s reason reaching the model verbatim and the model reporting it did not retry. On preToolUse a deny stops a write, a delete, and a read — the read before the file is opened.

ask.note: Real on two surfaces and absent on two others, and the difference decides how everything else is mapped. beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution raise the approval card — observed, with Skip / Always Run / Run. beforeReadFile has no ask at all, and preToolUse ACCEPTS one and silently allows the action: Cursor logs it as a valid response, merges it, shows nothing, and the tool runs. So on the file surfaces LeastGrant never emits ask; a floored action is refused and an unfamiliar one is allowed.

onCrash.note: Observed with failClosed: true as the installer writes it. A handler pointed at a script that does not exist blocked the call, and the model was told "Cursor blocked the terminal tool because a hook failed closed: ... returned no output."

onTimeout.note: Follows from failClosed on the gating events. Per-script timeout defaults to 60s.

timeoutDefaultSeconds.note: Per-script `timeout` in seconds; a warning is emitted above 3600.

canFailClosed.note: The installer sets failClosed: true on all three before* gates and it was observed doing what it says.

shell.note: beforeShellExecution fires before the command, and afterShellExecution after it. Round trip measured at 97–105 ms.

fileRead.note: Gated, as of the preToolUse layer — this was `observed` and is no longer. preToolUse fires for Read with `{file_path}` and NO content, before the file is opened. Measured: denying a credential read there meant beforeReadFile was never requested at all and the bytes were never loaded. The old route is still registered as a second layer for reads that do not go through the Read tool, and on that route the payload does arrive with the file already loaded.

fileWrite.note: Gated, as of the preToolUse layer — this was `none` and is no longer. preToolUse fires for Write with `{file_path, content}` and a deny stops the write. Verified live on the file that decides whether LeastGrant runs at all: an edit to <repo>/.cursor/hooks.json was refused and the file was unchanged, with the model reporting it would not work around the block.

fileDelete.note: Gated, and refused. Cursor reports tool_name "Delete" with {file_path}, and the engine marks every delete gap.blast — more than it will ever approve on its own, meaning a person must decide — exactly as it does for a shell rm. This surface has no way to reach a person, so the faithful translation is a refusal. Agent-initiated deletes therefore do not happen on Cursor through the file tools; a terminal rm goes through beforeShellExecution, which prompts. Before the generic gate they reached no hook at all and simply happened.

postToolUse.note: afterShellExecution and afterMCPExecution fire and are registered by the installer. LeastGrant answers them with no output, which Cursor logs as "produced no output" and treats as no opinion — correct for an after event, which cannot change anything.

exposesMode.note: No approval-mode field in any hook payload, although Cursor does have approvalMode internally (allowlist, unrestricted, auto-review).

modes.askSurvivesNote: On the two events that support it, an ask beats even the most permissive approval mode.

upstreamLimitations: preToolUse accepts `ask` and silently allows the action. Cursor logs the response as valid and merges it, no prompt appears, and the tool runs. Only allow and deny are enforced on that surface, so LeastGrant refuses a floored file action rather than pretending a person was consulted.

beforeReadFile is post-execution: its payload carries the file content, so a deny there suppresses what reaches the model without preventing the read. It is kept as a second layer behind preToolUse, which does prevent it.
No permission mode reaches the hook, so LeastGrant cannot tell an attended session from an unattended one.

Cursor has its own sandbox and its own auto-run flow, both acting before the user sees anything. A command may be attempted sandboxed, blocked by that sandbox, and retried unsandboxed, with LeastGrant consulted separately each time.
Cursor also ingests Claude Code hooks from .claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.json, so installing both adapters may double-fire.

Cursor’s generic step is spelled `preToolUse` and Claude Code’s is `PreToolUse`. Case-folded they are the same string, so a shared dispatcher will answer one in the other’s wire format unless it routes on the agent first.
There is no equivalent of Antigravity’s force_ask: nothing LeastGrant can return compels a prompt the host’s own settings cannot satisfy.

preToolUse has no ask, so any verdict the engine will not auto-approve — gap.blast, a tainted session, a previously refused action — becomes a refusal rather than a prompt. Only allow and deny are enforced there.
leastgrantLimitations: MCP has never been exercised live. beforeMCPExecution is registered and was never invoked, so its behaviour is contract-derived.

The generic gate is scoped by matcher to the file tools. Cursor was observed sending Read, Write and Delete; the matcher also covers Edit, MultiEdit, ApplyPatch, StrReplace, SearchReplace, CreateFile, DeleteFile, Move and Rename, which have not been observed and are covered against a rename upstream rather than because they were seen.
Verified on Windows only. The POSIX transport passes the payload on native stdin rather than through PowerShell and has not been exercised.
The hook timeout was not tested; only the crash path was.

Agent-initiated deletes through Cursor’s file tools are refused outright, not prompted. The engine says every delete needs a person and this surface cannot produce one, so refusing is the honest translation — but it is stricter than before the generic gate existed, when deletes were invisible. The refusal message points at the terminal, where a prompt does appear.

live.what: Two human-assisted rounds through the real IDE 3.18.25 on a disposable workspace with a synthetic .env. Round one established that Cursor loads ~/.cursor/hooks.json and registers its steps (from its own log), that an ask raises the approval card on beforeShellExecution, that a deny outranks the host’s auto-run flow and reaches the model verbatim, and that failClosed blocks when the handler cannot run. Round two established the generic preToolUse gate: it is registrable locally and fires; Write arrives with {file_path, content} and a deny stops the write; Delete arrives with {file_path} and a deny stops the delete; Read arrives with {file_path} and NO content, and denying it means beforeReadFile is never requested and the file is never opened; `ask` there is accepted, merged and silently allowed; and the matcher scopes, so a shell command fires only beforeShellExecution. Confirmed end to end with the shipped adapter, including a refused edit to the hooks file that decides whether LeastGrant runs.

transport.what: Observed rather than reproduced. Cursor delivers the payload through PowerShell with a UTF-8 BOM — first bytes ef bb bf on every captured invocation — which is the bug that once had LeastGrant refusing every Cursor tool call. Parsed correctly throughout, 87–105 ms round trip. preToolUse carries tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, conversation_id, generation_id, model, session_id, cursor_version, workspace_roots, user_email and transcript_path; beforeReadFile adds content and attachments; afterShellExecution adds output and duration.

contract.what: The 21-step event list, response validator, failClosed handling and the post-execution nature of beforeReadFile read from the shipped 42 MB workbench and extension-host bundles.

mechanism: Per-step command hooks in ~/.cursor/hooks.json. Six steps: the generic `preToolUse` scoped by matcher to the file tools, the three specialised gates, and two after* events for learning. On Windows the payload is delivered through PowerShell from a temp file rather than on stdin, prefixed with a UTF-8 BOM.

controlPaths.what: rules files a later session follows
